title: Launch gate orchestration and comm templates for high-risk feature rollouts
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Purpose: create a single-orchestrated launch gate and communications bundle for high-risk feature launches (examples: model architecture changes, KV cache behavior changes, dedicated capacity migration). Scope includes: release blockers checklist, decision authority matrix, automated pre-launch validations, staged rollout constraints, explicit rollback triggers, and pre-written incident/rollback communication templates for internal and external audiences. Goal: eliminate ambiguity during critical windows, reduce mean time to decision, and ensure consistent external comms when incidents occur.
checklist: Pre-launch engineering sign-off: perf benchmarks >= baseline and no new 95th pct regressions
SRE readiness: runbook uploaded to incident channel and playbook verified in staging
Security & compliance clearance: KMS/HSM checklist passed
Observable gating: alerts configured for latency, error rate, model output drift
Docs & release notes drafted and reviewed by Docs/Legal
Support runbook & triage doc published with canned responses
Rollback artifact validated: rollback automation tested in staging (can revert model/version and routing policies)
decision_authority: PM (launch owner): final go/no-go for customer-facing rollout
Eng Lead: technical risk assessment and feasibility of on-the-fly fixes
SRE Lead: operational readiness and availability guarantees
Legal/Security: block if compliance issues discovered
VP Product or designate: tie-breaker for cross-team disputes
release_blocker_criteria: Critical perf regression: 95th pct tail latency increase > 20% vs baseline
Error rate spike: sustained error rate > 1% for > 10 minutes after warmup
Model quality regression: automated eval F1 drop > 5% on benchmark prompts
Data leak or PII discovered in outputs
Rollback automation failing validation in staging
rollback_triggers_and_steps: Trigger - severe latency or outages: initiate immediate rollback to previous model/version via routing policy and DNS fallback
Step 1 - Notify stakeholders on #launch-alerts and page SRE on-call
Step 2 - Execute automated rollback pipeline; confirm KV cache invalidation where necessary
Step 3 - Run smoke tests against rollback target; verify request success and latency thresholds
Step 4 - Draft external comms (see templates) and hold 15-minute stakeholder bridge
Step 5 - Postmortem: ownership assigned, blameless timeline captured within 48h
incident_comm_templates: External P0 outage template: short statement of impact, affected endpoints, probable cause (if known), mitigation in progress, ETA for next update (30-60m), link to status page

External degraded performance template: describe user impact (e.g., increased latency), recommended workarounds (e.g., smaller requests, reduced concurrency), expected time to resolution, link to docs
Internal rapid-update template: timestamp, short summary, actions taken, immediate next steps, responsible owners, channels where bridge is happening
Rollback notice template: reason for rollback, user-facing behavior changes, guidance for customers on data or session impacts, contact for support
acceptance_criteria: A single launch-checklist artifact exists and is referenced by all teams
Automated gating tests run as part of CI with pass/fail recorded in the launch board
Incident templates approved by comms and legal and published in Support KB
Rollback executed successfully in staging within 10 minutes in 3 consecutive rehearsals
Stakeholder playbook (PM/Eng/SRE/Support) reviewed in 1 sync and sign-offs recorded
